The `_tool_manager.get_tool(...).fn` pattern is established: also used in tests/unit/test_profiles.py, test_server.py and test_memory_admin_tools.py (6 occurrences in 4 files). The tools in src/sqllens/server.py (get_profile 797, upsert_profile 831, delete_profile 883) are plain `@mcp.tool(structured_output=False)` functions, and the name and auth checks run inside the function bodies. The only wire-path step that calling `fn` skips is FastMCP's pydantic argument-type validation. The test passes a `str` name and a `dict` knobs (test lines 44-45, 79-81), which already match the signatures `name: str` and `knobs: dict[str, Any]`, so that step would reject nothing. The claim's literal 'no validation' is slightly broader than this, but it holds for every input the tests use. I did not read the FastMCP package itself. This rests on the standard FastMCP behavior that argument validation is the only step outside `fn`.
